items.title: chain (stage) inlay hints DOUBLE UP on an element's head chain - at kolt views.vl:110's `<button title("…") on:contextmenu(…) .styled(const icon_button_style(…)) .child(swap(…)) />` each `.styled`/`.child` line carries its ` as T` stage hint twice, and the opening `<button` tag carries a type hint of its own (three hints for one element); the element desugar is not a chain the reader wrote, so its stages should hint at most once per line - recommended: not at all inside an element head, nor on the opening tag
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-10-12/13): "chain hints doubling up on element tags (triple if you count the inlay hint on the opening tag). See views.vl:110"; E278 (a hint per STAGE of a chain split one stage per line - `program.stage_hints`, read in `Document::inlay_hints` at document.rs ~4833); element-syntax S5 (the markup desugar: `ElementHeadItem::Chain` items become method stages on the element builder; document.rs ~1491 `collect_markup_spans`, ~1530 where the desugar's `<tag` accessor is already SUPPRESSED from one editor surface - the precedent); E302 (the opt-in changes-only strategy would hide the repeats as a side effect, but the cause is at the mint); E121 (the keystroke inlay row)
items.body: Premise to verify first with the kolt line (a kolt copy carrying `src/lucide`): which two mints carry the same span - the desugar most likely lowers each head chain item into a stage whose span is the item's AND leaves the written `.styled(..)` call as a stage of its own (two `stage_hints` entries at one line end), while the opening tag's binding (the element temporary the desugar introduces) gets the ordinary `: T` binding hint. Then: (a) an element head's chain items mint NO stage hints and the desugar's element temporary mints NO binding hint - the element's type is its tag, every stage returns it, and the markup is not a chain the reader wrote (the same rule that suppresses the `<tag` accessor at ~1530); (b) if the owner wants the stages hinted, at most ONE per line, deduplicated at the mint by span, never on the opening tag. Rec: (a). A chain INSIDE an attribute value (`.child(swap(..).derive(..))` split over lines) keeps E278's hints - it is a chain. Pins: the kolt shape (zero hints on the element's head lines and the tag; the inner `swap` chain still hinted where split), a plain element with no chain items (unchanged), a chain on a builder that is NOT markup (E278's pins stand), the `inlay` keystroke row unchanged. Sizing S (the analyzer's stage-hint mint for `ElementHeadItem::Chain` + the element temporary's hint; vilan-lsp pins).
